title: Private Deployments: VPC / On‑Prem Deployment, Day‑2 Ops, Upgrade & Rollback, and Customer Requirements Library
author: Anika Shah
content:
Overview

Purpose: This document consolidates Redwood Inference's recommended playbook for private deployments (VPC and on‑prem), including reference architectures, on‑prem packaging guidance, production day‑2 operations, and explicit upgrade and rollback procedures. It also enumerates the customer requirements library used during pre‑sales and onboarding.

Scope: Applies to all private deployments of the Redwood control plane and serving runtime (Dedicated or Private SKU). It covers network and security requirements, packaging formats, operational tasks, maintenance windows, and incident/rollback procedures for releases of the runtime and orchestration.

Owners and contacts
- Primary owner: eng-private-deployments (eng team)
- Runbook oncall: platform-sre@redwood.internal
- Escalation: Head of Private Deployments (Diego Perez) -> Eng Director -> CTO

Summary of recommended flow
1) Pre‑sales / requirements capture (customer requirements library)
2) Packaging & delivery (VPC / on‑prem)
3) Initial deployment and validation
4) Day‑2 operations (monitoring, backups, capacity, incident handling)
5) Planned upgrades and rollback process

Reference architectures (high level)
- Small (single-region, HA across 2 AZs): 3 controller nodes (k8s control plane or VMs), 4 GPU hosts (in 2 AZs), shared NFS for persistent artifacts, Redis for caching, and Vault/KMS for secrets.
- Medium (multi-region active/passive): 5 controller nodes, 8 GPU hosts, cross‑region replication for artifacts, multi‑region DB (read replicas), and region failover playbook.
- Large (enterprise on‑prem): Dedicated HSM/KMS, air‑gapped option with package repository mirror, private image registry, and operator install with offline manifests.

Key SLOs and production thresholds
- Serving latency P95 target: <= 200ms for standard models; target <= 100ms for small models (customer tier dependent).
- Uptime: 99.95% for Dedicated private deployments (SLA customers).
- Backup RPO: 1 hour for model artifacts and config; RTO: <= 2 hours for control plane restore (documented runbook).
- Prometheus scrape interval: 15s; alerting thresholds defined below.

Networking & security requirements (VPC)
- Minimum: 3 private subnets across 2 AZs, NAT gateway for outbound control plane updates (optional), route tables segmented for management and data plane.
- Required ports (examples):
  - 443 TCP (control plane API)
  - 22 TCP (bastion/maintenance - restricted)
  - 6379 TCP (Redis) internal only
  - 5432 TCP (Postgres) internal only
- CIDR planning: Avoid 10.0.0.0/16 collisions with customer networks if using VPN; prefer 10.8.0.0/16 for private deployment to minimize overlap.
- Hybrid connectivity: Support for AWS Direct Connect / Azure ExpressRoute / on‑prem VPN.
- Secrets: Integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS, Azure KeyVault) or provide HSM appliance for on‑prem.

On‑prem packaging and installation options
- Packaging formats provided:
  - Kubernetes operator manifests + Helm chart (recommended)
  - Kustomize overlays for air‑gapped installs
  - Systemd + containerd bundles for non‑Kubernetes installs
  - Offline tarball with package repository mirror for air‑gapped environments

Example Helm values snippet (recommended defaults):

apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: redwood-values-example
data:
  values.yaml: |
    replicaCount: 3
    persistence:
      enabled: true
      storageClass: gp2
    runtime:
      gpuEnabled: true
      kvCacheSizeMb: 1024
    monitoring:
      prometheus: true
      alertmanager: true

Packaging checklist
- Signed images + SBOM included in release bundle.
- Offline repository URL + integrity SHA256 manifest.
- Installation preflight script (checks: kernel modules, nvidia drivers, container runtime, available disk, entropy).
- Postinstall validation suite (unit smoke tests, e2e model serve test).

Initial deployment validation (post‑install)
- Verify service health endpoints: /health and /ready on all control plane nodes.
- Run smoke generation test: 10 requests per second for 5 minutes against a small model; expect 99% success and latency within SLOs.
- Validate KV cache warmup: check cache hit ratio >= 30% on first 1 hour of steady traffic.

Day‑2 operations
- Monitoring & alerts (sample list):
  - Control plane down (alert if > 2 replicas fail)
  - Serving host GPU memory pressure > 85% (warning) / 95% (critical)
  - Request error rate > 1% sustained for 10m
  - KV cache eviction rate spikes > baseline * 3
  - Redis replication lag > 5s
- Scheduled maintenance: weekly non‑peak patch window (customer agreed), monthly capacity review.
- Backups: automated DB snapshots every hour, config and artifacts archived daily (encrypted at rest).
- Runbook references: see runbooks/restore-control-plane (internal link) for full restore steps.

Operational playbooks (examples)
1) Add capacity
   - Validate current utilization via Grafana dashboard (model_tokens/sec, GPU_util)
   - Submit scaling request to Dedicated autoscaler: kubectl scale deployment/serving --replicas=N
   - Validate load distribution and latency for 30m
2) Replace a failed GPU host (rolling procedure)
   - Cordon node: kubectl cordon <node>
   - Migrate pods: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data
   - Replace hardware and rejoin node, run preflight checks, uncordon.

Upgrade and rollback procedures
- Scope: Applies to runtime micro‑releases (patch/minor) and control plane releases. Major architectural changes require a separate upgrade plan and longer maintenance window.

Pre‑upgrade checklist (must be completed before any upgrade):
- Confirm maintenance window and notify customer (72h notice for major, 24h for patch).
- Verify successful backups (DB snapshot + artifacts) and store snapshot IDs.
- Verify cluster health: all pods ready, no evicted pods, CPU < 70% avg, GPU util < 70% avg.
- Ensure at least one compatible backup image exists for rollback.

Rolling upgrade procedure (Kubernetes operator / Helm)
1) Bump chart version and add the release notes to /releases.
2) Apply canary to 1 replica in non‑critical pool: helm upgrade --install redwood --namespace redwood -f values-canary.yaml ./chart
3) Run smoke tests against canary for 15‑30 minutes (see smoke test script: tools/smoke/run_smoke.sh).
4) If canary succeeds, perform rolling upgrade with maxUnavailable=1 and maxSurge=1 across control plane and serving nodes:
   - kubectl set image deployment/redwood-runtime redwood-runtime=<new-image-tag> -n redwood
   - Monitor pods status and logs; wait 5 minutes between each pod replacement by checking readiness probes.
5) After completion, validate end‑to‑end: sample workload (10qps for 10m) and customer testcases.

Rollback procedure (fast rollback)
- Trigger if canary or rolling upgrade causes: increased error rate > 1% sustained for 10m, P95 latency regression > 25% of baseline, or critical crashlooping pods.
Steps:
 1) Abort further rollouts and set cluster to maintenance mode (traffic routing to fallback model variant or fallback region).
 2) Revert Helm release to previous revision: helm rollback redwood <previous‑rev> -n redwood
 3) If immediate helm rollback fails or partial state is inconsistent, restore from snapshot:
    - Restore Postgres DB from snapshot ID <snapshot-id> using customer cloud provider console or internal restore job.
    - Re-deploy previous images: kubectl set image deployment/redwood-runtime redwood-runtime=<previous-image-tag> -n redwood
 4) Run validation smoke suite; re-enable traffic only after P95 and error rate are within thresholds.
 5) Postmortem: create an incident record and link to release (include logs, diffs, and timeline).

Air‑gapped / offline upgrade notes
- Deliverable: offline bundle containing images, operator manifests, SBOM, and signature file.
- Customer runs preflight which verifies checksums and image signatures.
- Upgrade is performed by applying manifests in sequence; automation wrapper scripts are included to preserve ordering and verify postinstall checks.

Customer requirements library (example checklist for onboarding)
- Legal & compliance: Data residency, required certifications (SOC2, ISO27001), encryption at rest requirement.
- Network: Allowed outbound endpoints, required inbound ports, preferred CIDR ranges, dedicated VPC/VLAN.
- Hardware: GPU type (A100/V100/H100), minimum host memory, local NVMe scratch space sizing.
- Identity & access: SSO provider (Okta/Azure AD), required RBAC roles, SCIM provisioning or manual user mapping.
- Key management: Customer KMS endpoint, HSM requirements, whether Redwood manages keys or customer manages keys.
- Maintenance: Approved maintenance windows, notification channels, and escalation contacts.
- Backup & retention: Required retention windows, legal hold processes.

Templates and artifacts included with release
- preflight.sh (bash script)
- postinstall-validate.sh (smoke test harness)
- offline-bundle.tar.gz (for air‑gap installs)
- sbom.json and signatures (for all images)
- helm charts and kustomize overlays (versioned)

Audit & compliance evidence
- All private deployments should enable audit logging to a customer‑managed S3 or file server.
- Retention policy defaults to 90 days; extendable per customer contract.

Change log
- 2026-09-15: Document created (initial consolidation of guides).
- 2026-10-12: Added detailed upgrade/rollback steps, air‑gap notes, and packaging checklist.

Appendix A — Quick commands
- Health: curl -sS https://<control-plane>/health | jq .
- Smoke: ./tools/smoke/run_smoke.sh --target https://<endpoint> --qps 10 --duration 600
- Backup verify: ./tools/backup/verify_snapshot.sh --id <snapshot-id>

Appendix B — Escalation & postmortem template
1) Summary of impact
2) Timeline of events with timestamps
3) Root cause analysis
4) Mitigations implemented
5) Action items and owners with deadlines

End of document
